newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Credit Suisse reports big loss, says 1997 starts well.
newsitem.headline: Credit Suisse reports big loss, says 1997 starts well.

text.p: Credit Suisse Group, after reporting a 2.43 billion Swiss franc ($1.6 billion) 1996 loss, said on Wednesday the current year had begun on a positive note.
"The year 1997 has begun positively, and we are therefore very confident of our ability to reach the goals we have set," the company said in a statement released ahead of a news conference.
But it also said that it had a good deal of work ahead, especially in quickly transforming the meaasures it had already adopted into lasting cost reductions.
Credit Suisse Group said it expected structural improvement in earnings power this year.
"For the current year Credit Suisse Group expects structural improvements in earning power throughout the group and, in particular, in Swiss business," it said in a statement on 1996 results.
It quoted new chief executive officer Lukas Muehlemann, who took the post on January 1 under a major reorganisation at the bank group, as outlining a number of main goals for 1997.

It said these goals were "an increase in profitability in all business areas, a continuation of the rapid and systematic implementation of the refocusing measures and the completion of the remaining restructuring projects on schedule".
It said Muehlemann also pledged to pursue systematically the selective expansion of activities in attractive markets and product areas.
"Strategic collaboration with Winterthur Insurance and Swiss Re will also be further expanded," the statements aid without elaborating.
